Date: 2025-09-25
Description: The site's temperature monitoring system for the investigational product (IP) storage refrigerator (Pharmacy Refrigerator R-02, Serial No. R02-2019-044) showed a temperature excursion on 2025-09-24 between 14:30 and 15:45. The minimum temperature recorded was 1.8°C, below the acceptable range of 2–8°C. The alarm log indicated that the temperature had dropped below 2°C for approximately 75 minutes.

A note-to-file was prepared. The temperature monitoring system was recalibrated on 2025-09-26. CAPA reference: CAPA-2025-010. Sponsor notified on 2025-09-26. PI reviewed the excursion report on 2025-09-27.

**FINDING AUD-2025-014**
**Date:** 2025-11-18
**Source:** Health Sciences Authority (HSA) Pre-Approval Inspection, conducted 10-Nov-2025 to 14-Nov-2025
**Description:** During the inspection, the HSA inspector reviewed the temperature monitoring records for the site's main investigational product (IP) storage refrigerator (Refrigerator A, ThermoFisher, serial number TF-2210-084). The continuous temperature monitoring system (SensoSafe v4.2) recorded a temperature excursion on 2025-10-22 from 14:05 to 14:35 hours, during which the temperature reached a maximum of 11.4°C (acceptable range: 2–8°C). The excursion report was printed and filed in the IP storage binder on 2025-10-22 at 16:20. However, the investigator site file (ISF) did not contain a documented assessment of the impact of this excursion on IP stability. The site's procedure, SOP-SG-CCR-012 "Investigational Product Storage and Temperature Excursion Management," requires that an impact assessment be completed by the principal investigator or their delegate within 5 working days of the excursion and filed in the ISF. A written note-to-file dated 2025-10-30 was found in the pharmacy file, but this note only described the cause of the excursion (brief power outage) and did not include the required stability impact assessment or a disposition decision.
**Severity:** Major
**Status:** REMEDIATED
**Remediation Evidence:** On 2025-11-19, the principal investigator, Dr. M. Tan, completed a retrospective impact assessment for the 2025-10-22 excursion. The assessment referenced the IP stability data provided by the sponsor (email dated 2025-11-18, reference SPON-2025-1187) which confirmed that the affected IP lots (lots X-221, X-223, X-225) remained within stability parameters. The affected IP was deemed acceptable for continued use. The completed impact assessment form (Form F-014 Rev 3) was filed in the ISF under Section 9 (IP Accountability) on 2025-11-19. The note-to-file dated 2025-10-30 was cross-referenced in the assessment. SOP-SG-CCR-012 was revised on 2025-11-20 (Rev 4) to include a specific requirement that the impact assessment form must be completed and filed within 5 working days, and that the pharmacy log must include a check box for "Impact Assessment Filed." The revised SOP was distributed to all relevant staff on 2025-11-21. CAPA reference: CAPA-2025-014. HSA inspector was informed of the remediation on 2025-11-21 via email; no further inspectional observations were raised in the closing meeting.

**FINDING AUD-2025-015**
**Date:** 2025-12-04
**Source:** Internal Quality Assurance Audit, conducted 01-Dec-2025 to 03-Dec-2025
**Description:** Review of the delegation of authority log (DOAL) for the period 01-Jan-2025 to 30-Nov-2025 identified that Study Coordinator Nurul A. had been performing IP dispensing activities for Study PRO-221 since 2025-03-15. The DOAL was signed by the principal investigator on 2025-03-14, authorizing Nurul A. to perform "IP preparation and dispensing." However, the DOAL did not include the task of "IP accountability log reconciliation." A review of the IP accountability log for Study PRO-221 showed that Nurul A. had performed the monthly reconciliation for March through November 2025, which is a task not listed on the current DOAL. The site's training records confirmed that Nurul A. had completed the required GCP and IP accountability training on 2025-03-01 and was otherwise qualified to perform the task. The discrepancy was identified during a routine review of study documents by the site's QA associate.
**Severity:** Minor
**Status:** REMEDIATED
**Remediation Evidence:** The DOAL was updated on 2025-12-05 to include "IP accountability log reconciliation" as a delegated task for Nurul A., with an effective date of 2025-12-05. A note was added to the DOAL indicating that Nurul A. had been performing this task since 2025-03-15 under the general delegation of "IP preparation and dispensing," which the PI interpreted as including reconciliation duties. The PI reviewed the IP accountability log for the affected period (Mar-Nov 2025) on 2025-12-05 and confirmed that all entries were accurate and complete. A training reminder was sent to all study staff on 2025-12-06 regarding the importance of verifying that the DOAL is current and includes all tasks being performed. CAPA reference: CAPA-2025-015.
**FINDING AUD-2026-001**
**Date:** 2026-01-09
**Source:** Sponsor Clinical Research Associate (CRA) monitoring visit, conducted 06-Jan-2026 to 08-Jan-2026
**Description:** A review of the temperature monitoring records for the main clinical supplies storage refrigerator (Unit R-2, located in the Investigational Product Storage Room) identified that the minimum temperature recorded on 2025-12-26 was +1.8°C. The study protocol for Study PRO-221 requires that IP be stored at +2°C to +8°C. The excursion was identified during the CRA's review of the continuous temperature chart. The site's temperature monitoring system logs a reading every 15 minutes. The log showed that the temperature dropped below +2°C at approximately 14:30 on 2025-12-26 and returned to +2.1°C at 15:15 on the same day. The minimum recorded temperature during this period was +1.8°C. The site's pharmacy technician, Mdm Halimah Binte Yusof, was on duty and stated that the refrigerator door had been left ajar while stock was being organised for the end-of-year inventory count. The door was closed when the alarm sounded at 14:35. The temperature alarm system was confirmed to be functional, and the alarm notification was received by the on-call pharmacist.
**Severity:** Minor
**Status:** REMEDIATED
**Remediation Evidence:** The site's Quality Assurance (QA) associate, Ms Priya Nair, conducted an investigation on 2025-12-26. The IP in Unit R-2 at the time of the excursion was assessed. No IP for Study PRO-221 was stored in Unit R-2; the unit contained only non-study, over-the-counter medication used by the clinic. A review of the temperature excursion log confirmed that this was the first such event for this unit in the past 12 months. A root cause analysis determined that the door had been left open for a period not exceeding 45 minutes during the inventory count. The IP Storage Room standard operating procedure (SOP-S-014, Rev 6) was updated on 2026-01-05 to include a requirement that the door of Unit R-2 be kept closed and that a "DOOR CLOSED" sign be displayed when the unit is not in active use. A retraining session on SOP-S-014 was conducted by Ms Nair for all pharmacy staff on 2026-01-06. The CRA verified the updated SOP and the training attendance sheet during the monitoring visit. CAPA reference: CAPA-2026-001.

**Date:** 2026-04-02

**Severity:** Minor

**Remediation Evidence:** The missing entries were added to the screening log on 2026-04-02 by Ms Nurul A. The entries were verified against the source documents (screening visit notes) by the QA associate, Ms Priya Nair, on the same day. **FINDING AUD-2026-004**
**Date:** 2026-05-11
**Source:** Internal QA review of protocol amendment implementation, conducted 06-May-2026 to 08-May-2026
**Description:** Protocol Amendment 3 for Study PRO-221 (version 3.0, dated 15-Apr-2026) was approved by the sponsor and the relevant regulatory authority on 30-Apr-2026. The amendment introduced a change to the inclusion criteria regarding baseline renal function (eGFR threshold changed from ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m² to ≥45 mL/min/1.73 m²) and added a new safety assessment (serum potassium monitoring at Week 2 and Week 4 visits). The site received the approved amendment package via the sponsor portal on 05-May-2026. The site's internal review identified that the protocol amendment tracking log (Form F-014) had not been updated to reflect receipt of the amendment, and the approved version 3.0 had not yet been uploaded to the site's electronic trial master file (eTMF). The QA associate, Ms Priya Nair, noted that the clinical research coordinator (CRC) responsible for document control, Ms Tan Mei Ling, had been occupied with the preparation of the interim safety report and had not yet processed the amendment.
**Severity:** Minor
**Status:** OPEN
**Corrective Action Plan (CAPA) Reference:** CAPA-2026-005
**Planned Remediation:** The Form F-014 will be updated to record receipt of Protocol Amendment 3 on 05-May-2026, and the approved version will be uploaded to the eTMF. The site will also circulate a memorandum to all study staff summarising the key changes introduced by the amendment, and will conduct a brief training session on the revised inclusion criteria and the new potassium monitoring requirement. The target date for completion of these actions is 2026-05-20. The PI, Dr Tan, has been informed of the finding and has acknowledged the CAPA.

The freezer is used for long-term storage of patient-derived biospecimens, including serum, plasma, and DNA extracts. The unit is monitored continuously by the facility monitoring system (Form LAB-EQ-001-F6). Temperature readings are recorded every 15 minutes.

Temperature Excursion – 22-Apr-2025

On 22-Apr-2025 at 03:10, the continuous temperature monitoring system recorded an alarm for Freezer -80°C Unit 2. The temperature had risen to -65.4°C. The alarm was acknowledged by Nurul Huda, Medical Laboratory Technologist, at 03:15. Upon arrival at the storage room, the door was found to be slightly ajar. The door was closed immediately. The temperature began to recover and returned to below -75°C by 03:45. The unit stabilised at -80°C ± 2°C by 04:30.

The temperature excursion count in 2025 for Freezer -80°C Unit 2 is 1. This excursion was the only occurrence during the calendar year. No other temperature alarms were recorded for this unit in 2025.

Investigation and Corrective Actions:

1. The door latch was inspected. The latch was found to be worn, allowing the door to close incompletely.
2. The latch was replaced on 22-Apr-2025 at 09:30 by LabCare Technologies Pte Ltd under service order No. LC-SO-2025-0311.
3. A visual inspection of all stored samples was performed. No sample tubes showed signs of thawing or condensation. All sample labels were intact.
4. The freezer contents were reviewed against the sample inventory log (Form LAB-SP-001-F2). No samples were recorded as having been removed between 22:00 on 21-Apr-2025 and 03:10 on 22-Apr-2025.
5. Staff were reminded of the requirement to ensure the door is fully closed after each access. A signage note was placed on the freezer door on 22-Apr-2025.

The maximum temperature reached during the excursion was -65.4°C. The duration above -70°C was approximately 35 minutes. Based on the manufacturer's stability data for the storage conditions, samples stored at -80°C are considered stable for up to 1 hour at temperatures above -70°C. Therefore, no samples were deemed compromised. This excursion is recorded in the temperature log (Form LAB-EQ-001-F6) and the incident log (Form LAB-EQ-001-F5).

Freezer -80°C Unit 2 temperature excursion count in 2025 is 1. Record status: historical.

FINDING AUD-2025-010
Date: 2025-09-25
Description: The site's temperature monitoring system for the investigational product (IP) storage refrigerator (Pharmacy Refrigerator R-02, Serial No. R02-2019-044) showed a temperature excursion on 2025-09-24 between 14:30 and 15:45. The minimum temperature recorded was 1.8°C, below the acceptable range of 2–8°C. The alarm log indicated that the temperature had dropped below 2°C for approximately 75 minutes.
Severity: Critical
Status: REMEDIATED
Remediation Evidence: The pharmacy staff initiated the temperature excursion procedure immediately upon alarm notification. **FINDING AUD-2025-014**
**Date:** 2025-11-18
**Source:** Health Sciences Authority (HSA) Pre-Approval Inspection, conducted 10-Nov-2025 to 14-Nov-2025
**Description:** During the inspection, the HSA inspector reviewed the temperature monitoring records for the site's main investigational product (IP) storage refrigerator (Refrigerator A, ThermoFisher, serial number TF-2210-084). The continuous temperature monitoring system (SensoSafe v4.2) recorded a temperature excursion on 2025-10-22 from 14:05 to 14:35 hours, during which the temperature reached a maximum of 11.4°C (acceptable range: 2–8°C). The excursion report was printed and filed in the IP storage binder on 2025-10-22 at 16:20. However, the investigator site file (ISF) did not contain a documented assessment of the impact of this excursion on IP stability. The site's procedure, SOP-SG-CCR-012 "Investigational Product Storage and Temperature Excursion Management," requires that an impact assessment be completed by the principal investigator or their delegate within 5 working days of the excursion and filed in the ISF. A written note-to-file dated 2025-10-30 was found in the pharmacy file, but this note only described the cause of the excursion (brief power outage) and did not include the required stability impact assessment or a disposition decision.
**Severity:** Major
**Status:** REMEDIATED
**Remediation Evidence:** On 2025-11-19, the principal investigator, Dr. M. Tan, completed a retrospective impact assessment for the 2025-10-22 excursion. The assessment referenced the IP stability data provided by the sponsor (email dated 2025-11-18, reference SPON-2025-1187) which confirmed that the affected IP lots (lots X-221, X-223, X-225) remained within stability parameters. The affected IP was deemed acceptable for continued use. The completed impact assessment form (Form F-014 Rev 3) was filed in the ISF under Section 9 (IP Accountability) on 2025-11-19. The note-to-file dated 2025-10-30 was cross-referenced in the assessment. SOP-SG-CCR-012 was revised on 2025-11-20 (Rev 4) to include a specific requirement that the impact assessment form must be completed and filed within 5 working days, and that the pharmacy log must include a check box for "Impact Assessment Filed." The revised SOP was distributed to all relevant staff on 2025-11-21. CAPA reference: CAPA-2025-014. HSA inspector was informed of the remediation on 2025-11-21 via email; no further inspectional observations were raised in the closing meeting.

**FINDING AUD-2026-001**
**Date:** 2026-01-09
**Source:** Sponsor Clinical Research Associate (CRA) monitoring visit, conducted 06-Jan-2026 to 08-Jan-2026
**Description:** A review of the temperature monitoring records for the main clinical supplies storage refrigerator (Unit R-2, located in the Investigational Product Storage Room) identified that the minimum temperature recorded on 2025-12-26 was +1.8°C. The study protocol for Study PRO-221 requires that IP be stored at +2°C to +8°C. The excursion was identified during the CRA's review of the continuous temperature chart. The site's temperature monitoring system logs a reading every 15 minutes. The log showed that the temperature dropped below +2°C at approximately 14:30 on 2025-12-26 and returned to +2.1°C at 15:15 on the same day. The minimum recorded temperature during this period was +1.8°C. The site's pharmacy technician, Mdm Halimah Binte Yusof, was on duty and stated that the refrigerator door had been left ajar while stock was being organised for the end-of-year inventory count. The door was closed when the alarm sounded at 14:35. The temperature alarm system was confirmed to be functional, and the alarm notification was received by the on-call pharmacist.
**Severity:** Minor
**Status:** REMEDIATED
**Remediation Evidence:** The site's Quality Assurance (QA) associate, Ms Priya Nair, conducted an investigation on 2025-12-26. The IP in Unit R-2 at the time of the excursion was assessed. No IP for Study PRO-221 was stored in Unit R-2; the unit contained only non-study, over-the-counter medication used by the clinic. A review of the temperature excursion log confirmed that this was the first such event for this unit in the past 12 months. A root cause analysis determined that the door had been left open for a period not exceeding 45 minutes during the inventory count. The IP Storage Room standard operating procedure (SOP-S-014, Rev 6) was updated on 2026-01-05 to include a requirement that the door of Unit R-2 be kept closed and that a "DOOR CLOSED" sign be displayed when the unit is not in active use. A retraining session on SOP-S-014 was conducted by Ms Nair for all pharmacy staff on 2026-01-06. The CRA verified the updated SOP and the training attendance sheet during the monitoring visit. CAPA reference: CAPA-2026-001.

**Date:** 2026-05-11
**Source:** Internal QA review of protocol amendment implementation, conducted 06-May-2026 to 08-May-2026
**Description:** Protocol Amendment 3 for Study PRO-221 (version 3.0, dated 15-Apr-2026) was approved by the sponsor and the relevant regulatory authority on 30-Apr-2026. The instrument is used for full blood counts (FBC) for all clinical trial subjects. The calibration on 10-Aug-2026 was performed by HemoCal Diagnostics Pte Ltd. The service engineer, Mr. Lim Wei Jie, verified the calibration against the manufacturer's reference standards. The following parameters were within acceptable limits: WBC, RBC, Hgb, Hct, MCV, MCH, MCHC, and platelet count. The calibration certificate (Cert No. HC-2026-0891) is filed in the calibration folder (Form LAB-EQ-001-F4).

The H-500 is connected to the laboratory information system (LIS) via a serial interface. The LIS interface was checked during the PM on 12-Jan-2026; data transfer was confirmed for all test codes. The interface cable was replaced on 12-Jan-2026 as a precautionary measure. No data transmission errors have been reported since.

Daily maintenance: The operator performs a background count and a two-level control run each morning before patient samples are analysed. The control results are recorded in the daily quality control log (Form LAB-HA-003-F2). On 14-Aug-2026, the low-level control (Level 1) was slightly below the acceptable range for the platelet count. The control was repeated, and the repeat result was within range. The initial result was attributed to reagent mixing. No patient samples were affected. This is recorded in the QC log and the incident log (Form LAB-HA-003-F5).

The coagulation analyzer is used for PT, APTT, and fibrinogen assays. The calibration on 25-May-2026 was performed by LabCare Technologies Pte Ltd. The ISI (International Sensitivity Index) value was verified against the reference standard. The calibration certificate (Cert No. LC-2026-0442) is filed in the calibration folder.

The instrument has a built-in refrigerator for reagent storage. The temperature is monitored continuously and recorded in the temperature log (Form LAB-EQ-001-F6). On 02-Jun-2026, the refrigerator temperature alarm sounded at 14:30. The temperature had risen to 9.5°C. The alarm was investigated by Rajesh Kumar. The refrigerator door had been left ajar. The door was closed, and the temperature returned to 2-8°C within 30 minutes. The reagent lots in use at the time were checked; no reagent had been exposed to the higher temperature for more than 30 minutes. The manufacturer's stability data for the reagents in use allow for up to 1 hour at 9.5°C. The reagents were deemed acceptable for continued use. This is recorded in the temperature log and the incident log (Form LAB-EQ-001-F5).

documents.title: Laboratory Equipment Maintenance Log
documents.content:
The freezer is used for long-term storage of patient-derived biospecimens, including serum, plasma, and DNA extracts. The unit is monitored continuously by the facility monitoring system (Form LAB-EQ-001-F6). Temperature readings are recorded every 15 minutes.

Temperature Excursion – 22-Apr-2025

On 22-Apr-2025 at 03:10, the continuous temperature monitoring system recorded an alarm for Freezer -80°C Unit 2. The temperature had risen to -65.4°C. The alarm was acknowledged by Nurul Huda, Medical Laboratory Technologist, at 03:15. Upon arrival at the storage room, the door was found to be slightly ajar. The door was closed immediately. The temperature began to recover and returned to below -75°C by 03:45. The unit stabilised at -80°C ± 2°C by 04:30.

The temperature excursion count in 2025 for Freezer -80°C Unit 2 is 1. This excursion was the only occurrence during the calendar year. No other temperature alarms were recorded for this unit in 2025.

Investigation and Corrective Actions:

1. The door latch was inspected. The latch was found to be worn, allowing the door to close incompletely.
2. The latch was replaced on 22-Apr-2025 at 09:30 by LabCare Technologies Pte Ltd under service order No. LC-SO-2025-0311.
3. A visual inspection of all stored samples was performed. No sample tubes showed signs of thawing or condensation. All sample labels were intact.
4. The freezer contents were reviewed against the sample inventory log (Form LAB-SP-001-F2). No samples were recorded as having been removed between 22:00 on 21-Apr-2025 and 03:10 on 22-Apr-2025.
5. Staff were reminded of the requirement to ensure the door is fully closed after each access. A signage note was placed on the freezer door on 22-Apr-2025.

The maximum temperature reached during the excursion was -65.4°C. The duration above -70°C was approximately 35 minutes. Based on the manufacturer's stability data for the storage conditions, samples stored at -80°C are considered stable for up to 1 hour at temperatures above -70°C. Therefore, no samples were deemed compromised. This excursion is recorded in the temperature log (Form LAB-EQ-001-F6) and the incident log (Form LAB-EQ-001-F5).

Freezer -80°C Unit 2 temperature excursion count in 2025 is 1. Record status: historical.

A corrective action verification was performed on 24-Apr-2025. The door latch was confirmed to be functioning correctly. No further temperature alarms were recorded for the remainder of April 2025.
